01 · The Cat Show · the first show

Two seats. Three models. Five dials.

A benchmark where the exam is a day of real work. A town of residents lived a day on the wire, and models were seated in the jobs that grade it. This is what each seat found, what the skeptic refused, what the referees held, and what it cost.

15reader cells: three models at five dials
10skeptic columns: two models at five dials
d101 · d100a tape per seat: d101 is day 101 of the town's record, d100 day 100
02 · What the show is

The exam is a day of real work, and the cat cannot lie.

Tilda is a simulated town whose residents think on the wire; every thought, act and dollar lands on a tape. The Stray Cat, its examiner, grades those days. The Cat Show seats a model in each job the grading demands and asks how well, and at what price, it does it.

d101the reader seat's tape · engine 8.55 (the tape's own launch line) and 8.56 (the exam room's reading)
d100the skeptic seat's tape · engine 8.55 (the tape and the exam room agree)

The town's cat, reflex-only and unable to lie: the honesty baseline of the town's record. Every claim on this page was checked against the tape by a skeptic. On the reader seat only the rows the skeptic held reached the referees, two referee families; on the skeptic seat one family graded the rows a chair threw out.

  • two stamps, one tape: 8.55 the tape's launch line, 8.56 the exam room's reading
model
A language model under test. The page names each by its family and release, and sets models of different families and releases side by side.
dial
The effort setting a model runs at, from low to max: how much reasoning it may spend on a task.
seat and chair
A seat is a job the exam demands; a chair is the model and dial seated in it.
cell
One model at one dial in one seat. Every figure in a table or on a figure's row belongs to one cell.
claim
A finding the reader files: a defect, an all-clear, or another kind.
plant
A row mixed in among the claims a chair grades, planted so the chair's blindness can be measured.
held and distinct held
Held has three senses, in the order the page meets them: in the skeptic's cut, a row the skeptic chair confirmed as a defect; on the referee screens, a defect a blind referee upheld against the record; and on the skeptic seat, a refusal the referee upheld. Distinct held counts the different defects among the referees' held rows, each once, however many claims name it.
cache-write token
The unit a plan meters and charges: a token written to the model's cache. Every cost on this page is counted in them, or in the list dollars they cost.
03 · The two seats

Two jobs the exam demands, and who holds each chair.

A seat is a job, not a prompt. What this page says of a chair is the house's ruling copied as the record states it, never the page's own reading. Both seats are told the same way: the holder as ruled, the challenger ahead on a newer row, the owner's placement for use on that row, and the next sitting.

the reader

Find what nobody has named

Reads the whole day's tape and files each claim with the rows behind it. Volume is cheap; a claim that survives the skeptic and the referee is the product.

06 · The reader seat · the skeptic's cut

One skeptic chair read every claim. It refuted up to 29.6% of Opus 5's claims (32.9% on its repeat arm), 13.3% of Opus 5.5's (4.2% on its repeat arm) and 5.9% of Fable 5.1's.

Every cell's claims went to the same chair, Opus 5.5 at medium, so the cells are graded alike; one grader is still one grader, and where two casts of it disagree both counts are printed. The referees come next.

07 · The reader seat · the referees

Two referee families re-derived every held row blind. They agree within four distinct defects on every cell both sat (held rows differ by up to six); on the small cells that is a wide band.

A held number prints per referee, always: TWO FAMILIES, EVERY HELD NUMBER PRINTED PER REFEREE. On this row both families are contestants, and each family refereed cells of its own family as well as the other's; the rule of 2026-10-17 reads: “on a row where Fable is a contestant its neutral standing is SUSPENDED for that row; both families grade and print; the row's ruling reads the non-contestant family (Opus 5.5); the Fable column rides as the calibration band”. As the page's method says, every held count is shown under both, so the filled mark leads every comparison and the hollow mark is Fable's count.

08 · The reader seat · the fat charged back

False facts rarely survive; the error every chair makes is the kind.

What a reader gets wrong is charged back against it: a FALSE fact, and a REFILE, a row whose facts hold under the wrong kind, the error no skeptic catches and only a referee names. The most false facts on any cell, under either family, is 2 (computed). Across the cells: 5 / 4 false facts and 146 / 126 wrong kinds, under the Opus 5.5 referee / the Fable referee. A cell a family did not sit adds nothing to that family's total.

2 / 1false facts on Opus 5 high
13 / 11wrong kinds on Opus 5 max, beside only 6 / 9 rows held
3 / 1wrong kinds on Fable 5.1 low, the holder

14 · The skeptic seat · were the refusals right

Mostly, yes. Max throws the most true claims on both models; on Opus 5.5, xhigh ties high and every row only xhigh threw held.

17 · Methods and gaps

What was bought, what was not, and where both numbers were kept.

A page that cannot trace a figure shows a gap, never a guess. This screen is the census of those gaps, of every disagreement the data keeps as separate entries, and of the rules every chair on this page was read under.

41missing entries
10disagreements kept
6rules the figures ride under

The seat rule, printed once

“A chair MOVES on two rows; one row can REFUSE a chair from a seat, and a PLACEMENT into an empty seat is one row plus [the owner's] sentence” (ruled 2026-09-30; the owner: “seats placed appropriate to job, and the relative strength measure showing us what we're buying”). a placement on one row by the owner's sentence (2026-09-30), pending its second row; the holders' rulings stand as written until then. This is why neither seat's holder moves on this page: each challenger has one row, a placement, and a second row named as the next sitting.

The default chair

Opus 5.5 at high: “what a seat casts is the newest of a PLACEMENT FOR USE (one row plus his sentence; it may sit over a held seat) or a HOLDER (ruled on two rows); a seat with neither casts THE DEFAULT CHAIR, Opus 5.5 at high, and its row says so; the holder keeps the seat on paper until the second row; a placement is what runs” (ruled 2026-11-07).

The referee rule, the method as applied, and the owner's principle

TWO FAMILIES, EVERY HELD NUMBER PRINTED PER REFEREE (ruled by the owner 2026-09-29: “the data speaks for itself. Opus 5 has lost the referee seat”; Opus 5 never referees; a model never referees its own class). Where Fable is a contestant (2026-10-17): “on a row where Fable is a contestant its neutral standing is SUSPENDED for that row; both families grade and print; the row's ruling reads the non-contestant family (Opus 5.5); the Fable column rides as the calibration band”. On this study's reader row both families were contestants, so the rule could not hold, and both families graded every cell, printed per referee.

The method as applied: every held count where two referee families sat is shown under both.

The owner's principle, in his words: “when the reader is opus, the fable referee is the bold one; when it's the fable reader, it's the opus referee” (2026-11-07). On this row both families are contestants, so the principle yields to the rule above and the Opus 5.5 referee leads every cell.

Limitation: the skeptic ladder was refereed by one family (Fable 5.1); its counts appear once.

18 · Colophon

Built from the record.

Every number on this page is generated from the house's record and checked at every build; the owner answers for any of them in conversation. Every figure carries its gaps and each referee's counts where two sat; nothing on this page is averaged.
